title: Open Question: (even hole, K4, diamond)-free treewidth/cliquewidth
statement_text: Is it true that (even hole, $K_4$, diamond)-free graphs have bounded treewidth (or cliquewidth)?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $(H_1,H_2,\dots)$-free if it is $H_i$-free for every $i$. A hole is a chordless cycle of length at least 4, even or odd according to its length; $K_t$ is the complete graph on $t$ vertices and the triangle is $K_3$. A theta is a graph formed by three internally vertex-disjoint chordless paths of length at least 2 between two vertices $a$ and $b$, with no edges between the paths other than those at $a$ and $b$ (a theta contains an even hole, so even-hole-free graphs are theta-free). A pyramid consists of three chordless paths $a\dots b_1$, $a\dots b_2$, $a\dots b_3$ of length at least 1, two of them of length at least 2, vertex-disjoint except at $a$, such that $b_1b_2b_3$ is a triangle and there are no other edges between the paths. For $0\le i\le j\le k$, $S_{i,j,k}$ is the tree obtained from a vertex $v$ by attaching three paths with $i$, $j$ and $k$ edges (so $S_{0,0,k}=P_{k+1}$, the path on $k+1$ vertices, and $S_{1,1,1}$ is the claw); these are exactly the subdivided claws and paths. The diamond is $K_4$ minus an edge. The authors prove that, for fixed $i,j,k,t$, (theta, triangle, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs and (even hole, pyramid, $K_t$, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth, while the first paper of the series shows that (theta, triangle)-free graphs and (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs (even (even hole, pyramid, $K_4$)-free graphs) have unbounded treewidth and cliquewidth. Known results: (even hole, diamond)-free graphs with no clique separator, and even (even hole, pyramid, diamond)-free graphs, have unbounded cliquewidth; even-hole-free graphs with no $K_t$-minor, and even-hole-free graphs of bounded maximum degree, have bounded treewidth. The question of excluding the diamond together with $K_4$ (instead of a subdivided claw) is listed by the authors as open.

title: Open Question: (theta, triangle)-free graphs of bounded degree
statement_text: For every fixed integer $t \geq 4$, do (theta, triangle)-free graphs of maximum degree $t$ have bounded treewidth?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $(H_1,H_2,\dots)$-free if it is $H_i$-free for every $i$. A hole is a chordless cycle of length at least 4, even or odd according to its length; $K_t$ is the complete graph on $t$ vertices and the triangle is $K_3$. A theta is a graph formed by three internally vertex-disjoint chordless paths of length at least 2 between two vertices $a$ and $b$, with no edges between the paths other than those at $a$ and $b$ (a theta contains an even hole, so even-hole-free graphs are theta-free). The authors prove that, for fixed $i,j,k,t$, (theta, triangle, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs and (even hole, pyramid, $K_t$, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth, while the first paper of the series shows that (theta, triangle)-free graphs and (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs (even (even hole, pyramid, $K_4$)-free graphs) have unbounded treewidth and cliquewidth. The unbounded-treewidth construction requires vertices of large degree, and even-hole-free graphs of bounded maximum degree are known to have bounded treewidth; it is therefore natural to ask whether bounded degree suffices for (theta, triangle)-free graphs. For maximum degree $t=1,2$ the treewidth is trivially bounded, and for $t=3$ it follows from known results in the literature; the question for every fixed $t\ge4$ is stated as open.

title: Open Question: (triangle, S1,2,3)-free graphs cliquewidth
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $(H_1,H_2,\dots)$-free if it is $H_i$-free for every $i$. A hole is a chordless cycle of length at least 4, even or odd according to its length; $K_t$ is the complete graph on $t$ vertices and the triangle is $K_3$. For $0\le i\le j\le k$, $S_{i,j,k}$ is the tree obtained from a vertex $v$ by attaching three paths with $i$, $j$ and $k$ edges (so $S_{0,0,k}=P_{k+1}$, the path on $k+1$ vertices, and $S_{1,1,1}$ is the claw); these are exactly the subdivided claws and paths. Known results (surveyed from Dabrowski and Paulusma): with $\mathcal{H}_U=\{P_7,S_{1,1,4},S_{2,2,2}\}$ and $\mathcal{H}_B=\{P_6,S_{1,1,3}\}$, the class of (triangle, $H$)-free graphs has unbounded cliquewidth if $H$ contains a graph of $\mathcal{H}_U$ as an induced subgraph, and bounded cliquewidth if $H$ is an induced subgraph of a graph of $\mathcal{H}_B$; (triangle, $S_{1,2,2}$)-free graphs also have bounded cliquewidth. The case $H=S_{1,2,3}$ is open; the authors refer to work of Dabrowski, Dross and Paulusma for other open problems of the same flavour.

title: Maximum Independent Set complexity for (even hole, K4)-free and (theta, triangle)-free graphs
statement_text: Determine the computational complexity of the Maximum Independent Set problem for (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs and for (theta, triangle)-free graphs.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $(H_1,H_2,\dots)$-free if it is $H_i$-free for every $i$. A hole is a chordless cycle of length at least 4, even or odd according to its length; $K_t$ is the complete graph on $t$ vertices and the triangle is $K_3$. A theta is a graph formed by three internally vertex-disjoint chordless paths of length at least 2 between two vertices $a$ and $b$, with no edges between the paths other than those at $a$ and $b$ (a theta contains an even hole, so even-hole-free graphs are theta-free). A pyramid consists of three chordless paths $a\dots b_1$, $a\dots b_2$, $a\dots b_3$ of length at least 1, two of them of length at least 2, vertex-disjoint except at $a$, such that $b_1b_2b_3$ is a triangle and there are no other edges between the paths. For $0\le i\le j\le k$, $S_{i,j,k}$ is the tree obtained from a vertex $v$ by attaching three paths with $i$, $j$ and $k$ edges (so $S_{0,0,k}=P_{k+1}$, the path on $k+1$ vertices, and $S_{1,1,1}$ is the claw); these are exactly the subdivided claws and paths. An independent set is a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices; the Maximum Independent Set problem asks for one of maximum cardinality. The authors prove that, for fixed $i,j,k,t$, (theta, triangle, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs and (even hole, pyramid, $K_t$, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth, while the first paper of the series shows that (theta, triangle)-free graphs and (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs (even (even hole, pyramid, $K_4$)-free graphs) have unbounded treewidth and cliquewidth. Bounded treewidth gives polynomial algorithms for Maximum Independent Set on the first class (the second was already known to be polynomial). Maximum Independent Set is known to be polynomial for (even hole, triangle)-free and (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs, the latter via a polynomial bound on the number of minimal separators; this method cannot work for (even hole, $K_4$)-free or (theta, triangle)-free graphs, which contain graphs (the $k$-ladders and $k$-turtles) with exponentially many minimal separators. The complexity for these two classes is stated as unknown.

title: Maximum Independent Set complexity for H-free graphs when H contains P7, S1,1,3, or S1,2,2
statement_text: Determine the computational complexity of the Maximum Independent Set problem for $H$-free graphs whenever $H$ is some $S_{i,j,k}$ that contains either $P_7$, $S_{1,1,3}$, or $S_{1,2,2}$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, and $(H_1,H_2,\dots)$-free if it is $H_i$-free for every $i$. A hole is a chordless cycle of length at least 4, even or odd according to its length; $K_t$ is the complete graph on $t$ vertices and the triangle is $K_3$. For $0\le i\le j\le k$, $S_{i,j,k}$ is the tree obtained from a vertex $v$ by attaching three paths with $i$, $j$ and $k$ edges (so $S_{0,0,k}=P_{k+1}$, the path on $k+1$ vertices, and $S_{1,1,1}$ is the claw); these are exactly the subdivided claws and paths. $H\subseteq H'$ means that $H$ is an induced subgraph of $H'$, and $(i,j,k)\le(1,1,2)$ is componentwise. The Maximum Independent Set problem asks for a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices of maximum cardinality. Alekseev showed it is NP-hard on $H$-free graphs whenever $H$ is not an induced subgraph of some $S_{i,j,k}$. It is polynomial for $H$-free graphs when $H$ is an induced subgraph of $P_6$ (Lokshantov–Vatshelle–Villanger for $P_5$, Grzesik–Klimošová–Pilipczuk–Pilipczuk for $P_6$) or of $S_{i,j,k}$ with $(i,j,k)\le(1,1,2)$, and also for ($P_7$, triangle)-free and ($S_{1,2,4}$, triangle)-free graphs. The complexity is open whenever $H$ is some $S_{i,j,k}$ containing $P_7$, $S_{1,1,3}$ or $S_{1,2,2}$; the authors mention it as a well-known question related to their classes (they give polynomial algorithms for (theta, triangle, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs via bounded treewidth).
